name: Learn basic latte art
blurb: A heart, then a rosetta. Latte art is 80% milk texture — get glossy microfoam and the pouring is far easier than it looks.
gear: An espresso machine with a steam wand
A 350 ml pouring jug with a sharp spout
Practice patience: it wastes a lot of milk
steps: Steam the milk correctly: introduce air for the first few seconds only until the pitcher warms, then submerge the tip to create a smooth whirlpool.
Aim for glossy, paint-like microfoam with no visible bubbles, at about 60 °C. Swirl and tap the jug to fix small bubbles.
Pull a shot with good crema and swirl it so the surface is even.
Start pouring high and thin into the centre to mix, filling the cup to about two-thirds.
Drop the jug close to the surface and let the foam float on top — this is the moment the pattern appears.
For a heart, pour into one spot then cut straight through. For a rosetta, wiggle the jug side to side while drawing backwards, then cut through.
tips: Big bubbles mean you aerated too long or too deep. Stretch only for the first couple of seconds.
Pouring too high at the end buries the foam. Get the spout almost touching the crema.
Practise the pour with washing-up liquid and water in a jug to save milk.
proof: A clean, symmetrical heart three times in a row, and a recognisable rosetta.
